title: Time Based Key-Value Store
keyIdea: Store each key's (timestamp, value) pairs in a vector. Set timestamps only increase, so push_back keeps it sorted. get(key, t) = the last pair with time <= t: binary search, and on every time <= t save the value and go right (left = mid + 1); otherwise go left.

approaches.name: Scan back from the newest
approaches.idea: Same storage; get walks the key's list from the end and returns the first value with time <= t.
approaches.why: A get may walk the whole list for that key (up to 2·10⁵ calls → too slow in the worst case).

approaches.name: Binary search the timestamps
approaches.idea: left = 0, right = size − 1, ans = "". values[mid].first <= t → ans = value, left = mid + 1; else right = mid − 1.
approaches.why: Each get halves the list each step.

quiz.q: Why is each key's list sorted without ever sorting it?
options: set timestamps are strictly increasing, so push_back appends in time order

quiz.q: values[mid].first <= timestamp. Why left = mid + 1 and not stop?
options: mid is valid, but a later pair might still be <= timestamp, and we want the latest
To avoid an infinite loop only

quiz.q: get("love", 5) when the only sets were at times 10 and 20?
options: "": nothing was set at or before 5, so ans stays empty

quiz.q: Why auto& values = mp[key] and not auto values?
options: & avoids copying the whole vector on every get
